question.problem:
Find the shortest distance between the origin and the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=0$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{2}+\sqrt{2})\,i+(\sqrt{2}-{t}^{2})\,j+2t\,k \\ T(0) & =k \\ N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of the point where $t=0$ is

$$
p=r(0)=(0+\sqrt{2})\,i+(\sqrt{2}-0)\,j+0\,k=⟨\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2},0⟩.
$$

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(0)$ and the principal normal $N(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =T(0)\times N(0) \\  & =k\times (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-\,j)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance between our plane and the origin is given by

$$
d=\frac{|(p-0)\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=\frac{|p\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=|p\cdot n|,
$$

since $‖n‖=1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|p\cdot n| \\  & =|⟨\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2},0⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,1,0⟩| \\  & =|1+1| \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
